The UGV paper, titled "Collision Cone Control Barrier Functions for Kinematic Obstacle Avoidance in UGVs," proposes a new class of Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) aimed at helping Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) avoid collisions with kinematic (moving) obstacles. While existing CBFs have been effective for static obstacles, their application in dynamic environments has been limited. 

The authors introduce a novel CBF formulation that ensures the relative velocity of the vehicle is directed away from potential collisions with obstacles, effectively utilizing the collision cone approach. This approach provides theoretical guarantees for safety regarding both unicycle and bicycle models of UGVs.

The efficacy of this new control methodology was verified through simulations conducted on PyBullet, using platforms like TurtleBot3 and F1Tenth. The results demonstrated that the new CBF formulation significantly enhances the ability of UGVs to navigate safely in dynamic environments.
